title: Roles, permissions, and least privilege
goal_html: Students practice auditing role assignments against job functions and identifying least-privilege violations and candidates for role redesign. Ties to LO 5.2.A, 5.2.B.
steps_html:
1. Each group opens the simulation and reviews the fictional company's role assignments, flagging any user whose permissions exceed their job function before submitting.
  2. For each flagged user, the group writes one sentence naming the specific excess permission and the likely cause (privilege creep from a past project, an overly broad role, etc.).
  3. Groups redesign one over-broad role into two or more narrower roles and explain how the redesign reduces blast radius without blocking anyone's actual job.
collaborate_html: Assign roles: an "auditor" identifies the violation, a "role designer" proposes the narrower role split, and a "recorder" documents the before/after. Rotate roles for each flagged user.
exit_html: Each student submits: one flagged user + the excess permission + the proposed fix (remove permission or split role).
